answers.why: Israel's cattle are distinguished from Egypt's cattle during the plague.
Israel owns the spared cattle, and Pharaoh refuses to release the people.
The LORD distinguishes Egypt from Israel, whose people and beasts are protected.
Anyone eating leaven is cut off from the community of Israel.
Moses summons Israel's elders to give Passover instructions for their families.
Pharaoh identifies Israel as the people released from serving Egypt.
Israel is the camp before which the angel goes and behind which he moves.
The Egyptians flee from Israel because the LORD fights for them.
The LORD saves the people who crossed the sea from Egypt's power.
The rescued Israelites see the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
Israel sees the LORD's mighty work, and the same people fear and believe him.
Moses leads Israel from the sea, and they travel together through the wilderness.
